main_text.l: ex adverso, sed quasi ex transverso
inter se opponuntur. Itaque disparata non in-
commodè á nonnullis appellátur, quasi com-
parata sint, quæ directò inter se opponuntur.
Repugnátium enim alterum unum est è duo-
bus contrariis: alterum verò non aliud con-
quasi si duo gladiatores antagonistæ inter se
sive συμμαχὸν haberet: & alter è gladiatoribus
gnans dicitur, quod contrarij est consequens.
ratio est? Cùm inter Antecedens & Cósequés
duo cótraria: Amicus, Hostis. tū subiiciantur
quæ inter se quoq; contraria sunt. Cōtrariorū
enim (ut ait Cic.) cōtraria sunt cōsequētia. de-
inde amicus cū verbo lædendus cōmittatur:

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the decorated initial Q of QUONIAM is uncertain, so the letter is shown as an italic Q. Greek συμμαχὸν is read from the scan and marked as doubtful in spirit only; the accents may differ. A small bullet mark stands in the left margin near the second paragraph; it looks like a printer's or stain mark and is not transcribed. Long s has been normalised to s throughout, and u/v and i/j to the vowel/consonant forms. The printed "difparata" and "tranfuerso" are read as "disparata" and "transverso" under the long-s rule.
